GENERAL SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #4
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating ? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .

3. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Nitrogen gas only

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Reproduction? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Human Reproduction.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Reproduction.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Reproduction.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproduction.

5. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

10. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. watt (W)

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.

12. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.

14. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

15. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Thin Lenses ● Types of lenses ● Properties of thin lenses (principal focus, opti? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Thin Lenses ● Types of lenses ● Properties of thin lenses (principal focus, opti.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Thin Lenses ● Types of lenses ● Properties of thin lenses (principal focus, opti.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thin Lenses ● Types of lenses ● Properties of thin lenses (principal focus, opti.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Thin Lenses ● Types of lenses ● Properties of thin lenses (principal focus, opti.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain The Mole 2.3 Hydrocarbons 3.0 Natural Physical Science 3.1 Thin Lenses 3.2 Newto and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Thin Lenses ● Types of lenses ● Properties of thin lenses (principal focus, opti and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
